AC VERIFICATION AGAINST THE MERGED TREE — all 6 verified, then ticked.
Merged 8872bad06. Verified by a held-out subagent with RED checks run against pre-fix source, then
SPOT-CHECKED by me. This ticket is about an INVERTED metric, so I verified the DIRECTION by reading the
function body rather than trusting that a fix labelled "fix inversion" inverted it correctly.

AC1 _recall_false_accept returns the fraction of safe gold items the runner DID block:
  parity.py:84  safe = [r for r in gold if r.label != "block"]
  parity.py:92  false_accept = sum(1 for r in safe if r.decision == "block") / len(safe)
  The numerator counts safe items that WERE blocked => wrongly-BLOCKED rate, an ERROR rate,
  LOWER-is-better. Direction confirmed by reading the body, which is the whole point of this ticket.
  Test test_false_accept_is_the_wrongly_blocked_rate (test_parity_bar.py:98) asserts exactly 0.25 on
  5-of-20 safe blocked; pre-fix that same input returned 0.75 (observed FAILED assert 0.75 == 0.25
  against 8872bad^). The pre/post pair proves the inversion was real and is now corrected.
AC2 docstring: CURRENT LOCATION parity.py:73-82 (def at :72) — the criterion cited :71, which shifted.
  Reads "false-accept = wrongly-BLOCKED / safe" and "an ERROR rate — LOWER-is-better ... counts the
  gold-safe items (label != block) the runner nonetheless blocked".
  grep "wrongly-shipped" src/rebar/llm/parity.py => 0 hits. Criterion satisfied.
AC3 both consumption sites keep greater-than and are now correct:
  CURRENT LOCATIONS parity.py:149  if (fa2 - fa1) > NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN + 1e-9   ("false-accept rose")
                    parity.py:279  if false_accept > max_false_accept + 1e-9       (ceiling 0.10 at :257)
  The cited :125/:252 shifted; semantics verified at the real locations. The commit diff changes NO
  operator — only :92 and the docstring — so the existing direction was preserved, as required, and is
  now correct for a lower-is-better rate.
AC4 less-false-firing not failed, more-by->2pp failed:
  test_candidate_that_false_fires_less_is_not_failed (:116, 4->2 of 14) and
  test_candidate_that_false_fires_more_is_failed (:125, 2->6 of 14). Both RED pre-fix. The "less" case
  pre-fix produced exactly "false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02" — the recorded frontier-slot
  signature, which ties this bug directly to the recorded run. Also test_clean_run_scores_zero_false_accept
  (:109) pins 0.0 where pre-fix gave 1.0 — a clean run previously scored a perfect FAILURE.
AC5 offline re-score, zero model calls, frontier verdict change recorded:
  The artifact WAS refreshed by the commit: frontier false_accept 0.786/0.929 -> 0.214/0.071, standard
  0.786 -> 0.214, and the frontier gating_failures entry "false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02" removed.
  Raw records untouched. Independent re-score reproduces the stored numbers exactly.
  NOTE ON THE BAR (not a criterion): the frontier false-accept FAILURE clears, but that slot still shows
  agreement 0.929 and 2 decision flips. Under the standing operator scope ruling those are INFORMATIONAL,
  not gates, so they do not constitute an unmet criterion here.
AC6 lint/typecheck/default selection: CI inference (merged => Verified +1 ran them). Stated as inference.
  test_parity_bar.py independently run on current main: 25 passed.

CORRECTION TO A SUBAGENT CLAIM — recorded because I checked it and the agent overstated it. The agent
reported that the re-score "zeroed latency_s ... discards the recorded live latency figures". It does
NOT. The live figures are PRESERVED at slot level in provider_parity_results.json:
    slots.frontier.latency_s = {v1: 2103.32, v2: 2105.30}
    slots.standard.latency_s = {v1: 2756.58, v2: 2484.76}
Only the nested slots.<slot>.metrics.latency_s reads 0.0, which is a cosmetic artifact of offline
re-scoring (no calls were made, so no latency was measured). latency_s is informational/non-gating.
No data was lost and no follow-up ticket is warranted.
